use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The goal is to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The goal is to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation; C2 JU correlates them, thereby resolving the dual designation so the reported track represents a single data point.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Two ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The two eligible tracks have been correlated and the dual designation is resolved; the reported track represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Correlate the two eligible ballistic missile tracks reported to the interface.
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data from J2 messages to reduce surveillance track reporting redundancy.
Minimizing the general occurrence and duration of dual designations through section protocols.

claims.content: C2 JU
Two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The two tracks have passed the required number of correlation tests and restrictions (including positional criteria) before the correlation is executed.
The positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation have been extrapolated to the same time.
A C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation and initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

The C2 JU continuously correlates locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG; upon recognizing that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates the correlation-test process, either automatically or manually.

The C2 JU makes an automatic correlation test upon receipt of each remote real-time J3.2/J3.3 track not confirmed to have existing correlation, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation.
The same two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, the C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

The recognizing JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN selection, requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks; the message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation.
The C2 JU drops the Dropped TN, ceases reporting the track, and transmits the J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message on that track after the J7.2 message.
The dual designation is resolved: each ballistic missile track reported on the interface now represents a single data point.

Diverges from Step 6: The C2 JU may manually initiate correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or correlation requirements; however, two tracks shall not be manually correlated if they are of a different E/C, if one is simulated and the other is live, or if both are remote.

Diverges from Step 6: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator is alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 6: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a). If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile while the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
Diverges from Step 8: A C2 JU responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 8: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, the Dropped TN has an OCC, and RV is set to 3, the system executes the correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
Diverges from Step 9: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, the Dropped TN is retained as a remote track.
Diverges from Step 9: If the Identity of the Retained TN and Dropped TN are the same, associated identification data reported for the Retained TN shall be retained.

Diverges from Step 9: If the Identity or Identity Amplifying Descriptor of the Retained TN and Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD, the Dropped TN ID/IAD and Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type shall be transferred to the Retained TN.

missing_aspects: The claim states this exception applies 'despite the conflicting-ID restriction', but the cited evidence explicitly lists exceptions to restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) AND 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a). Paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) refers to engagement status messages, not necessarily ID conflicts alone. The specific link to 'conflicting-ID restriction' as the sole context is an inference not fully supported by the text which groups it with engagement status constraints.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 2: If the correlation test involves tracks arising from one of the situations most likely to lead to dual ballistic missile designations (initial report on ballistic missile contacts, track merging, simultaneous multiple launches, registration errors, time of observation differences, or high velocity contacts), the correlation may fail or produce erroneous results, triggering exception handling. Exit: correlation may fail or produce erroneous results; exception handling is triggered.

Diverges from Step 6: If a ballistic missile track is considered lost (the JU with R² has received no local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or the JU determines the track is lost by other system criteria) and is reported with the Lost Track Indicator field set to value 1, the JU reporting the Lost Track data is assumed to have a Track Quality of 5 less than the value being reported, so a JU holding Tracking data may assume R² with the calculated TQ. Exit: the tracking JU may assume R² at the calculated TQ.
Diverges from Step 5: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time. Exit: the correlation test is outside the permitted timing window.

Diverges from Step 8: Receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless prespecified conditions exist that require or allow rejection; the engagement-status exception to a correlation restriction shall not be applied by any JU upon receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message, and a JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message while holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation; whenever a correlation request is rejected, the rejecting JU transmits a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Exit: the correlation is rejected and the rejection is reported via J7.2 (RV=2).

Diverges from Step 10: If it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation should occur. Exit: track decorrelation is performed.
The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.

Receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN; if the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it has dropped the Dropped TN and transmitted the J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message after the J7.2 message.

Upon correlation execution, the Retained TN's data state includes the Dropped TN's Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track); any nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is transferred if the corresponding Retained TN data is zero.

Identification data transfer is complete according to ID conflict restrictions: if restricted and IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, specific ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred to the Retained TN.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV=3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 has no clear outcome. Its 'Exit: the correlation test is outside the permitted timing window' merely restates the triggering violation; it does not say whether the correlation test is aborted, fails, is retried, or returns to a main-flow step. This is not an explicit terminal failure/prevention state with no continuation claimed. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence/recovery/exit behavior that an invalid correlation test is not used for correlation.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 initiates the correlation-test process even though Precondition 2 already establishes that the two tracks have passed the required correlation tests and restrictions before the correlation is executed. Steps 4-6 then repeat the first and second tests, so the main flow restarts a completed eligibility process rather than continuing from the trigger's recognition/initiation to resolve the dual designation.

inconsistency_hints: Preconditions already establish that the two tracks are eligible and have passed the required correlation tests/restrictions, and the Trigger is the C2 JU recognizing that eligibility and initiating resolution. The main flow, however, starts with the broader continuous-correlation process and steps 1–5 re-run the correlation-test/eligibility phase (first tentative correlation, second test), and step 6 then restates the Trigger's initiation action. This restarts an earlier phase instead of continuing from the Trigger.

Exception flow claim 1 branches from Step 2 based on dual-designation-prone scenarios, but its stated exit is only 'exception handling is triggered.' This is not a concrete branch outcome: it does not return to a main-flow step, terminate or hand off to a defined process, or end in an explicit failure/prevention state. The cited evidence may support that those scenarios can cause correlation failure, but the claim does not define what exception handling does or where control continues.

Precondition claim 0 states the C2 JU has already recognized the two tracks as eligible, but that recognition is the Trigger event itself. A use case cannot have the actor already in the triggered state as a precondition; the recognition should be part of the Trigger (and Main Flow step 1), not an independent pre-existing state.

Precondition claim 1 states the tracks have already passed the required number of correlation tests and restrictions before the correlation is executed, but Main Flow steps 2-6 execute the first correlation test, tentative correlation, second correlation test, and only then initiate resolution. The Main Flow therefore restarts the test scenario after the Trigger instead of continuing to the resolution action; step 1 and step 6 both claim the resolution initiation, so the flow is not a clean continuation.
